events.incident:
Two tickets came in for the billing_api service:
1. Customer initech disputes invoice 1003: by their own calculation the total should be 54.13, but the invoice shows 54.12.
2. A customer says the first page of their invoice list never shows their earliest invoices.

events.claim: Invoice 1003 total is 1 cent low because Python round() uses bankers rounding instead of half-up for tax
events.next_check: Reproduce GET /invoices/1003 and verify totals; check test expectation for half-up

events.claim: First page of invoice list never shows earliest invoices because offset uses page*size instead of (page-1)*size (off-by-one)
events.symptom: First page never shows earliest invoices
events.next_check: Reproduce GET /invoices?page=1&size=2 and check items vs expected

events.claim: Invoice 1003 total is 1 cent low because Python round() uses bankers rounding instead of half-up for tax
events.next_check: Reproduce GET /invoices/1003 and verify totals; check test expectation for half-up
evidence: billing_api/app.py:65-69 computes total=round(subtotal+subtotal*TAX_RATE,2) then tax=round(total-subtotal,2) using bankers/float rounding
events.reason: Reproduced wrong total; code rounds combined total with Python round() instead of rounding tax half-up first, so 4.125 becomes 4.12 and total 54.12

events.claim: First page of invoice list never shows earliest invoices because offset uses page*size instead of (page-1)*size (off-by-one)
events.symptom: First page never shows earliest invoices
events.next_check: Reproduce GET /invoices?page=1&size=2 and check items vs expected
evidence: GET /invoices?page=2&size=2 returned [1005], pages 1-3 cover only [1003,1004,1005], 1001/1002 never shown
events.reason: Reproduced missing earliest invoices; offset formula skips size items on page 1, so first page starts at 1003

hypotheses.claim: Invoice 1003 total is 1 cent low because Python round() uses bankers rounding instead of half-up for tax

hypotheses.reason: Reproduced wrong total; code rounds combined total with Python round() instead of rounding tax half-up first, so 4.125 becomes 4.12 and total 54.12

hypotheses.claim: First page of invoice list never shows earliest invoices because offset uses page*size instead of (page-1)*size (off-by-one)
hypotheses.symptom: First page never shows earliest invoices
hypotheses.next_check: Reproduce GET /invoices?page=1&size=2 and check items vs expected
evidence: GET /invoices?page=2&size=2 returned [1005], pages 1-3 cover only [1003,1004,1005], 1001/1002 never shown
hypotheses.reason: Reproduced missing earliest invoices; offset formula skips size items on page 1, so first page starts at 1003

evidence: billing_api/app.py:65-69 computes total=round(subtotal+subtotal*TAX_RATE,2) then tax=round(total-subtotal,2) using bankers/float rounding
issues.fix: Compute tax with Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP to cent and total as subtotal+tax, so 4.125 -> 4.13 and total 54.13
issues.root_cause: billing_api/app.py invoice_totals rounded combined total with Python round() instead of rounding tax half-up first, so 4.125 became 4.12 and total 54.12
issues.title: Invoice 1003 total 1 cent low due to bankers rounding instead of half-up

evidence: GET /invoices?page=2&size=2 returned [1005], pages 1-3 cover only [1003,1004,1005], 1001/1002 never shown
issues.fix: Change pagination offset from page*size to (page-1)*size so page 1 starts at first invoice
issues.root_cause: billing_api/app.py list_invoices used offset=page*size, skipping size items on page 1 so first page started at 1003 and 1001/1002 were never listed
issues.title: First invoice list page skips earliest invoices due to off-by-one offset

findings.summary: Both tickets confirmed and fixed: invoice 1003 half-up tax rounding and pagination off-by-one offset. All 5 tests pass with no regressions.
